# Phase 4: Systems and infra topics the papers skip

*weeks 21–22, plus rapid-fire review* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p4)

Five topic clusters from Alisa's map have no paper in your curriculum but appear constantly in rapid-fire technical discussions. Each gets a reading, a small HAND implementation, and the specific question it is known to unlock.

| Cluster | Known interview question |
| --- | --- |
| [Tokenization](tokenization/) | "Time complexity of the merge step?" "Why does tokenizer efficiency shift the Chinchilla frontier?" |
| [Inference and the KV cache](inference-kv-cache/) | "70B model, 96 layers, d_model 8192, bf16, one 128K sequence — how much KV memory?" (~200 GB) |
| [Distributed training](distributed-training/) | "8 × 80 GB A100s, 70B model — walk me through memory math and parallelism strategy." "What is 5D parallelism?" |
| [Evaluation](evaluation/) | "How would you know if your model got better?" |
| [Data](data/) | "Design a filtering pipeline and tell me how you'd validate it." |

**The scaling book.** [How to Scale Your Model](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/) (Austin et al., Google DeepMind) is the reference for the infra cluster. Read chapters 1, 4, 5 and 7 in full and work the exercises; skim 2, 3 and 12 for notation; chapters 6 and 8 (training and serving Llama 3) are the worked examples to reproduce the arithmetic for on paper.


Sources: [alisa-roadmap README, Phase 1 and 2 sections](https://github.com/soasme/alisa-roadmap) · [CS336 Spring 2025](https://cs336.stanford.edu/spring2025/) · [How to Scale Your Model](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)
